title: A truth maintenance system
abstract: Introduces a truth-maintenance architecture that records justifications and dependencies for beliefs, detects contradictions, revises assumptions through dependency-directed backtracking, and preserves explanations for current beliefs.

title: Maintaining knowledge about temporal intervals
abstract: Develops an interval-based representation of time and a set of qualitative interval relations with constraint-propagation procedures for maintaining temporally consistent knowledge about events.

title: On the logic of theory change: Partial meet contraction and revision functions
abstract: Provides the foundational AGM account of rational belief contraction and revision, specifying postulates and constructions for incorporating information that may conflict with an existing belief set.

title: A Taxonomy of Time in Databases
abstract: Systematizes temporal dimensions used in database systems, including distinctions that became foundational for separating when a fact is valid in the modeled world from when it is stored or known by a database.
venue: ACM SIGMOD International Conference on Management of Data

title: An assumption-based TMS
abstract: Introduces the assumption-based truth maintenance system, representing propositions through sets of supporting assumptions so that multiple contexts, alternatives, and contradictions can be maintained without destructively retracting prior derivations.

title: Problem solving with the ATMS
abstract: Shows how an assumption-based truth maintenance system can support problem solving by maintaining alternative environments and their dependency structures while identifying inconsistent combinations of assumptions.

title: Temporal Databases
abstract: Presents database support for information whose truth or storage status varies over time and discusses temporal semantics that underpin later valid-time and transaction-time database models.

title: A logic-based calculus of events
abstract: Introduces the Event Calculus for reasoning explicitly about events, their effects, and time; its treatment permits later information about past events to revise conclusions about what holds.

title: On the difference between updating a knowledge base and revising it
abstract: Distinguishes belief revision, where new information corrects beliefs about a static world, from belief update, where the world itself has changed, and develops separate rationality principles for the two operations.
venue: Proceedings of the Second International Conference on Principles of Knowledge Representation and Reasoning (KR'91)

title: On the Semantics of Transaction Time and Valid Time in Bitemporal Databases
abstract: Develops formal semantics for transaction time and valid time in bitemporal databases, separating database-history time from the time during which modeled facts hold.
venue: New York University Working Paper IS-92-42

title: A synthetic view of belief revision with uncertain inputs in the framework of possibility theory
abstract: Studies belief revision when incoming information has graded uncertainty, distinguishing forms of uncertain input and expressing their effects through possibility-theoretic belief change.

title: On the logic of iterated belief revision
abstract: Extends belief-revision theory to sequences of observations by representing epistemic states and proposing constraints intended to preserve relevant conditional information across successive revisions.

title: Belief Revision with Unreliable Observations
abstract: Develops belief revision for observations that may themselves be noisy or unreliable, relaxing the assumption that every newly received observation must be accepted as true.

title: Why and Where: A Characterization of Data Provenance
abstract: Formalizes forms of database provenance that describe where output information came from and why it appears, providing mechanisms for retaining source and derivational dependencies.

title: TimeML: Robust Specification of Event and Temporal Expressions in Text
abstract: Defines a markup language for events, temporal expressions, and temporal links that can anchor events to times and relate events to one another while also representing aspects such as modality.
venue: AAAI Spring Symposium on New Directions in Question Answering

title: Weakening conflicting information for iterated revision and knowledge integration
abstract: Addresses conflicting information in iterated revision and knowledge integration by weakening inconsistent information rather than simply discarding it, allowing more of the evidence structure to survive conflict resolution.

title: On the revision of probabilistic beliefs using uncertain evidence
abstract: Studies principled revision of probabilistic beliefs when evidence is uncertain and examines how repeated uncertain observations should alter an existing probabilistic state.

title: SemEval-2007 Task 15: TempEval Temporal Relation Identification
abstract: Defines a shared evaluation for identifying temporal relations involving events and temporal expressions, helping establish benchmark formulations for event-time and event-event temporal relation extraction.

title: Classifying Temporal Relations Between Events
abstract: Investigates automatic classification of temporal relations between textual events using linguistic and contextual features rather than merely extracting standalone time expressions.

title: Provenance Semirings
abstract: Introduces an algebraic provenance framework in which annotations record derivational dependencies of query results, supporting non-destructive explanation of how conclusions depend on underlying data.
venue: ACM Symposium on Principles of Database Systems

title: Jointly Combining Implicit Constraints Improves Temporal Ordering
abstract: Uses global temporal constraints, including transitivity and information from normalized times, to improve event ordering beyond independent pairwise temporal decisions.

title: Finding Contradictions in Text
abstract: Develops a typology and detection approach for textual contradictions, showing the importance of event coreference, negation, antonymy, and other linguistic phenomena in determining when two statements conflict.

title: FactBank: a corpus annotated with event factuality
abstract: Introduces a corpus in which event mentions are annotated for factuality as commitments attributed to relevant sources, distinguishing factual, counterfactual, and uncertain assessments rather than assuming that every mentioned event occurred.

title: Commitment Tracking via the Reactive Event Calculus
abstract: Combines social-commitment semantics with a reactive Event Calculus procedure to track commitment status at runtime, including explicit temporal constraints and deadlines.

title: Provenance in Databases: Why, How, and Where
abstract: Surveys database provenance models for recording origins and derivations of data, including uses in explanation, debugging, trust, annotations, and reasoning about updates.

title: Temporal Information Extraction
abstract: Introduces a system for extracting temporally scoped facts and uses global inference over temporal constraints, including transitivity and bounds on event start and end times.
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence

title: A Logic-Based, Reactive Calculus of Events
abstract: Provides a reactive logic-based Event Calculus suitable for evolving event narratives, maintaining formally grounded conclusions as new events arrive rather than recomputing only through retrospective queries.

title: L.I.A.R.: Achieving Social Control in Open and Decentralized Multiagent Systems
abstract: Models observed interactions as locally maintained social commitments with explicit states and defines inconsistency among commitments, allowing different observers to hold incomplete or divergent views when messages or later changes are missed.

title: Monitoring time-aware commitments within agent-based simulation environments
abstract: Extends a commitment lifecycle with temporal transitions and compensation mechanisms and uses a reactive Event Calculus to monitor how commitments evolve during execution and whether they are honored.

title: Does It Happen? Multi-hop Path Structures for Event Factuality Prediction with Graph Transformer Networks
abstract: Models event factuality through multi-hop graph paths so that evidence affecting an event's factual status can be propagated across nonlocal linguistic structures.

title: Are You Sure That This Happened? Assessing the Factuality Degree of Events in Text
abstract: Models event factuality using polarity and epistemic certainty and assigns assessments relative to information sources, providing finer distinctions than binary occurred-versus-not-occurred labels.

title: Did It Happen? The Pragmatic Complexity of Veridicality Assessment
abstract: Studies judgments about whether events actually occurred and shows that veridicality depends not only on local lexical cues but also on pragmatic context and background knowledge.

title: Representing and monitoring social commitments using the event calculus
abstract: Formalizes commitment operations in a first-order Event Calculus with data and metric time and shows how the representation can be used for online monitoring of evolving social commitments.

title: SemEval-2013 Task 1: TempEval-3: Evaluating Time Expressions, Events, and Temporal Relations
abstract: Defines TempEval-3 evaluation tasks spanning event extraction, time expressions, and temporal relations, providing a benchmark for systems that bind events to times and to other events.

title: An Annotation Framework for Dense Event Ordering
abstract: Introduces a dense temporal annotation process designed to produce connected event-relation graphs, addressing sparsity that limits global temporal reasoning in earlier temporal corpora.

title: Dense Event Ordering with a Multi-Pass Architecture
abstract: Builds dense event-ordering graphs with a multi-pass architecture and uses temporal closure to infer additional relations, supporting document-level temporal structure rather than isolated pair classifications.
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: Cross-document event ordering through temporal, lexical and distributional knowledge
abstract: Combines event extraction, temporal relations, lexical information, distributional knowledge, and event coreference to order related events across multiple documents.

title: Integrating Deep Linguistic Features in Factuality Prediction over Unified Datasets
abstract: Unifies several event-factuality resources and evaluates factuality prediction with deep linguistic features on a common scale, helping connect previously separate factuality annotation schemes.

title: A Structured Learning Approach to Temporal Relation Extraction
abstract: Formulates temporal-relation extraction as structured prediction so that global dependencies and temporal consistency can influence relation decisions instead of classifying pairs independently.

title: A Multi-Axis Annotation Scheme for Event Temporal Relations
abstract: Proposes a multi-axis representation of temporal structure and start-point-focused annotations to reduce ambiguities in event temporal relations and better represent different temporal dimensions of events.

title: Neural Models of Factuality
abstract: Develops neural factuality models evaluated across multiple factuality datasets, treating event factuality as a graded semantic property rather than equating mention with occurrence.

title: Improving Temporal Relation Extraction with a Globally Acquired Statistical Resource
abstract: Augments local temporal-relation extraction with globally learned event-order statistics and structured inference to improve consistency and robustness of event ordering.

title: Joint Reasoning for Temporal and Causal Relations
abstract: Performs joint structured inference over temporal and causal event relations, exploiting constraints between the two relation types to obtain more globally coherent event interpretations.

title: Temporal Information Extraction by Predicting Relative Time-lines
abstract: Represents temporal information by predicting relative positions of event start and end points on a timeline, offering a structured alternative to independent categorical temporal-relation labels.

title: An Improved Neural Baseline for Temporal Relation Extraction
abstract: Combines contextual neural representations with temporal knowledge and global inference constraints to provide a stronger baseline for extracting event temporal relations.

title: Joint Event and Temporal Relation Extraction with Shared Representations and Structured Prediction
abstract: Jointly detects events and their temporal relations using shared representations and structured prediction, reducing the disconnect between deciding what constitutes an event and reasoning about its temporal placement.

title: Dynamically Updating Event Representations for Temporal Relation Classification with Multi-category Learning
abstract: Updates event representations dynamically using information from multiple temporal links, allowing temporal decisions about an event to influence its representation for subsequent relation classification.

title: Dialogue State Tracking with Incremental Reasoning
abstract: Tracks dialogue state gradually across turns using incremental reasoning and backend information, demonstrating a mechanism for accumulating and updating state as new conversational evidence arrives.
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: TIMEDIAL: Temporal Commonsense Reasoning in Dialog
abstract: Introduces a dialogue benchmark for temporal commonsense reasoning in which models must use conversational context to infer temporal relationships and constraints that are often implicit rather than explicitly timestamped.

title: Utilizing Relative Event Time to Enhance Event-Event Temporal Relation Extraction
abstract: Improves event-event temporal relation extraction by explicitly modeling relative event-time information, coupling event timing estimates with relation classification.

title: Maintenance of Social Commitments in Multiagent Systems
abstract: Formalizes maintenance commitments whose relevant states are intended to remain true and supplies rule-based operational semantics relating maintenance commitments, achievement commitments, and agents' goals.
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence

title: End-to-end event factuality prediction using directional labeled graph recurrent network
abstract: Presents an end-to-end model that detects event anchors and predicts their factuality jointly using a directional labeled graph recurrent network, reducing dependence on separately supplied event mentions.

title: RSP-DST: Revisable State Prediction for Dialogue State Tracking
abstract: Uses a two-stage dialogue-state process in which an initial state prediction is followed by a revising prediction based on conversational context, explicitly targeting errors that would otherwise propagate into later turns.

title: TeCre: A Novel Temporal Conflict Resolution Method Based on Temporal Knowledge Graph Embedding
abstract: Detects temporal conflicts in knowledge-graph facts using temporal embeddings and temporal constraints such as precedence, disjointness, and mutual exclusion, then applies a completion model to propose corrected facts.

title: More than Classification: A Unified Framework for Event Temporal Relation Extraction
abstract: Represents temporal relations as logical expressions over event start and end points, unifying extraction under a more compositional temporal representation than a flat multiclass label set.

title: Maintenance commitments: Conception, semantics, and coherence
abstract: Develops formal semantics and operational rules for maintenance commitments whose conditions must continue to hold, relating their lifecycle to achievement goals and commitments and analyzing coherence among those constructs.

title: Document-Level Event Factuality Identification via Reinforced Semantic Learning Network
abstract: Addresses document-level event factuality by selecting relevant sentences and tokens with hierarchical reinforcement learning before encoding the event and its broader document context, rather than relying only on sentence-local cues.
venue: Journal of Computer Science and Technology
